description: Shape of the complete GSTR-1 upload file: the wrapper the portal expects around the per-section payloads. Key ORDER is significant for byte-level comparison against the reference tool and is reproduced exactly as the official tool emits it.

provenance.source: The tool builds this wrapper by string concatenation in utility/common.js (formDataFormat), so the key order and the empty-value shapes below are literal.

notes: `version` is a literal tied to the tool release, not to the return.
`hash` is the literal four-character string 'hash' — a placeholder the tool never fills in. Confirmed against a captured file.
`gt` and `cur_gt` (aggregate turnover) appear immediately after `fp` and only when a numeric turnover is supplied.
`hsn` changes shape with the return period: a single `data` array before 05-2025, and `hsn_b2b` / `hsn_b2c` arrays from 05-2025 onward.

EMPTY SECTIONS ARE OMITTED. The key list below is the working file's template, but the upload file passes through omit-empty, so a section with no records is absent entirely rather than present as []. An empty return therefore carries only gstin, fp, version and hash. Confirmed by diffing a file captured from the running tool.
`hsnSac` is in the working-file template but, being always empty, never survives into the upload file.
A numeric 0 survives omit-empty, so `csamt: 0` is emitted rather than dropped.

omit-empty is recursive, so an empty member of a nested object is dropped too — an HSN summary with only a B2B half emits `hsn: {hsn_b2b: [...]}` with no `hsn_b2c` key. Verified against a file captured from the tool for exactly that case: a workbook with the B2C half left blank produced a one-member `hsn` object, and this implementation reproduces it byte for byte.

THE ADJUSTMENT TABLES ARE RENAMED IN THE UPLOAD FILE. `atadj` becomes `txpd` and `atadja` becomes `txpda`, and because the rename is a plain assignment of a key the template never declared, the two renamed sections are appended AFTER every other section — past `hsn` and the e-commerce blocks — rather than keeping their original position. The originals are set to `[]` and then dropped by omit-empty. Reading the working-file template alone gives both the wrong key names and the wrong position; verified against a captured file.

A QUARTERLY FILER'S FIRST TWO MONTHS ARE AN IFF, NOT A FULL RETURN. Only b2b, b2ba, cdnr, cdnra, ecom and ecoma survive alongside the four header keys; everything else, gt and cur_gt included, is deleted. See the `iff` block.

filename.description: The tool names the file from the date it was GENERATED, not the return period: day, month and four-digit year concatenated with no zero padding (26 July 2026 gives '2672026'). Confirmed against a file captured from the running tool.

chunking.description: The tool writes a single file iff the size it measures is strictly under 4.7 MiB (4.7 * 1024 * 1024 = 4928307.2, a float compared with <; offline.js:5474) — not the 5 MB the portal documentation mentions. The measure is jsonSize(JSON.stringify(gstfile)) over an ALREADY-SERIALIZED string: the body's UTF-8 length plus two enclosing quotes plus one escape byte per '"' and '\' in it, so real files split at roughly 3.9-4.1 MiB of actual JSON. At every integer measure, m <= 4928307 is equivalent to the reference's m < 4928307.2. There is NO item-count limit anywhere in the tool; the widely cited 19,000-invoice figure is portal folklore.

part_filename.description: DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE. The reference names chunks returns_<dmy>_R1_<gstin>_offline_<secKey|others>_<random 1..100000>.json (utility/common.js exports.chunk) — a Math.random() suffix that can collide and silently overwrite a chunk, and is literally '_others_undefined.json' on one path. Parts here are numbered deterministically instead. The single-file name is unchanged and byte-identical.

reference_defects: The splitter re-serializes the whole accumulated chunk after every record it packs — O(n^2) in file size; the route disables the HTTP timeout to survive it.
Only b2b, b2ba, b2cl, b2cla and cdnr split at record granularity, and their records are packed in REVERSE document order.
Every chunk after the first accumulator flush LOSES the header: gstin, fp, gt, cur_gt, version and hash are zeroed and then removed by omit-empty, leaving chunks the portal cannot accept.
An oversized section outside the five splittable ones is silently DROPPED from the output.
A second oversized splittable section throws inside a swallowed catch and the request hangs forever.
One code path writes byte-identical duplicate chunk files, which the portal would reject as duplicate invoices.
chunking.divergence: DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from the reference splitter (precedent: the b2cl/b2cla blank-cess note in fixtures/golden/README.md). The trigger and the size measure are faithful; the split itself is correct by design instead of bug-for-bug, because the reference's chunked output is unusable for its own purpose: every part here is an independent complete payload carrying the full header (gstin, fp, gt/cur_gt when supplied, version, hash); sections pack in envelope key order and split at ENVELOPE granularity; the union of all parts' section contents equals the unsplit file; every part fits the measured limit; bodies and names are deterministic. A single envelope too large to fit a part alone is a hard error, never a silent drop.

iff.description: A quarterly (QRMP) filer submits an Invoice Furnishing Facility return in the first two months of each quarter, and it carries only these keys. The reference deletes every other top-level key outright (offline.js:5464), including gt and cur_gt, when isTPQ is set and the period's month is not a multiple of 3. Introduced in release 3.0.0 and applicable from 1 January 2021.

keys.description: Present in the working-file template but always emptied before the upload file is written: the tool moves this section's records to txpd/txpda and assigns [] here, so omit-empty always drops it. The records themselves are emitted under the renamed key at the end of the file.

Advances adjusted. Renamed from atadj on the way out, which is why it sits at the end: the assignment creates a new key, and a new key is appended after every key the template declared.
Amended advances adjusted. Renamed from atadja, and appended for the same reason as txpd.
